title: Dynamic Escort Scheduler for token bursts and comm coalescence
creator: Maya Chen
description: We see intermittent 10-60ms tail latency spikes for multi-GPU short-chunk workloads (short prefill followed by decode) when token bursts align poorly with NCCL schedules. This ticket proposes a lightweight run-time escort scheduler that temporarily escorts token bursts through a coalescing window to improve NCCL overlap and reduce kernel handoff stalls without requiring heavy cross-stage rebalancing.
background: Production traces show that short-lived prefill+decode requests create microbursts that either (a) trigger small NCCL collectives repeatedly, or (b) idle stages waiting for last-token handoffs. Existing approaches (static rendezvous windows or coarse microbatching) either increase latency for single-token queries or are too heavy for dynamic load. We need an adaptive in-runtime mechanism that detects burst patterns and opportunistically coalesces communication without impacting steady-state throughput.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Dynamic Escort Scheduler with three components: (1) Burst Detector: lightweight EWMA-based detector at the request ingress that tags requests likely to form microbursts; (2) Escort Queue & Window: short-lived per-stage escort queue that holds tagged tokens for a configurable micro-window (e.g., 0.5-3ms) to permit NCCL coalescing and batch-friendly kernel selection; (3) Kernel Hinting & Fallbacks: runtime emits kernel-selection hints based on queued token depth and expected sequence length to pick fusion-friendly attention kernels and prefetch KV cache ranges. The escort window is adaptive: it grows slightly when NCCL small-collective rate is high and shrinks otherwise. If windowing would violate per-request latency SLO (configurable), we bypass escorting and fall back to existing path. We will implement escort scheduling as an opt-in runtime flag and add observability + metrics to measure impact.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Escort scheduler can be toggled per-deployment; 2) On canary (dedicated pool), observed reduction in NCCL small-collective count by >=25% for short-chunk workloads; 3) p99 latency for single-token chat queries does not regress by more than 5ms; 4) Kernel selection logs show increased use of fused attention kernels for escorted bursts; 5) No memory leaks or regressions in KV cache correctness.

risks: Added per-request queuing could increase single-request latency if misconfigured
Incorrect kernel hints may degrade throughput for long sequences
Interplay with autoscaling: holding tokens briefly may affect utilization and scaling signals
Complexity of coordination across tensor/pipeline stages could introduce deadlock if windows misaligned
open_questions: What is the default escort window range that balances coalescing vs latency? (0.5-3ms proposed)
Should escort decision be based solely on ingress heuristics or also on downstream stage load telemetry?
How to expose controls in Console for per-route escort policy and SLO guardrails?
Can we leverage existing NCCL stream priorities or do we need a custom communicator wrapper?
